{{Quote|We are not Separatists trying to leave the Republic, we are Loyalists trying to preserve democracy in the Republic.|Mon Mothma|audio=MonMothmaRationalizesTreason-ROTS-DVD2.flac|<ref name="rots">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
'''Mon Mothma''', a native of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] who served as an important political figure from the waning days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], one of the founders of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], and the first [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. When the [[Declaration of a New Order|foundation]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] replaced the Republic that had existed for many millennia, she met with her allies in the Senate, such as [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] and [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]].

In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], she signed the [[Corellian Treaty]], along with Organa, [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], and [[Galen Marek]], in order to form the Alliance to Restore the Republic. She, along with the others, were taken captive aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star I]], although they were [[Battle on Death Star I|rescued]].

Mothma played an important role in the ensuing [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and after the decisive Rebel victory at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], she became the first Chief of State of the newly founded New Republic. She also had a daughter, [[Lieda Mothma|Lieda]], and a son, [[Jobin]]. Mothma passed away peacefully in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|I find that making my home over in the image of where I lived in better times is good for my sanity.|Mon Mothma, recalling the image of her childhood environment|<ref name="X-Wing: The Krytos Trap">''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Chandrila-AoRCR.png|thumb|right|250px|Mon Mothma's homeworld: Chandrila]]
The [[Chandrilan/Legends|Chandrilan]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] Mon Mothma was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in [[48 BBY/Legends|48 BBY]] into a wealthy and influential [[Mothma family/Legends|family]] on the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]<ref name="Coruscant and the Core Worlds" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]].<ref name="EGC" /> It was considered that she had been destined to play a major role in the fate of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> Mon's [[Parent/Legends|mother]], [[Tanis Mothma]], served as [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of [[Hanna City/Legends|Hanna City]], the world's [[Capital/Legends|capital]],<ref name="Coruscant and the Core Worlds" /> while her [[Mon Mothma's father/Legends|father]] was an [[Arbiter-general/Legends|arbiter-general]] who worked for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> Mon grew up in peaceful times in Hanna City on the shores of the [[Silver Sea/Legends|Silver Sea]], which she developed a love for.<ref name="X-Wing: The Krytos Trap" /> She learned leadership, administration, governmental organization,<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook" /> and a love for her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] from her mother. Her father showed her the wonders of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> and she learned about diplomacy and the abilities to listen and compromise from him.<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook" /> Upon the [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|election]] of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Naboo crisis]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Mothma distrusted him, perceiving what she felt was an evil gleam in his [[Eye/Legends|eye]] when his election was announced.<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook" /> 

===Senator===
{{Quote|Madam Speaker, it is obvious that my learned friend from Alderaan refuses to acknowledge the peril in which we find ourselves. If we do not take bold, definitive action — and quickly — this great Republic will die, or worse, will be transformed into something foul and evil. We must act now to preserve the principles upon which this Republic was founded!|Mon Mothma, debating Bail Organa in the Galactic Senate prior to the downfall of the Republic|<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />}}
[[File:MonMothma2.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Mon Mothma as a young senator]]
During the [[Great Peace of the Republic]], Mon was elected by the people of Chandrila to be their [[Senator/Legends|senator]]<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> while she was still a teenager.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> It was considered a natural progression for her, and at the [[Time/Legends|time]] she was the youngest person to have ever been elected senator.<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook" /> Mothma foresaw the decline of the Republic and was a young firebrand on the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] floor, advocating for rapid expansion and growth for the Republic with visionary plans that some considered wildly impractical. She developed a friendly rivalry with the veteran fellow Core Worlds Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], who had a more pragmatic approach and worked behind the scenes to maintain order. During one debate in the Senate, Mothma argued passionately for the preservation of the Republic's principles, while Organa argued that the senators required a smaller-scale approach to fix issues that could be addressed. Mothma criticized Organa for metaphorically attempting to repair plumbing while a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] descended into a [[Star/Legends|sun]], to which Organa replied that it was preferable than doing nothing.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Mon's distrust of Palpatine alienated her from many of his puppet allies.<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> Despite their rivalry, Organa and Mothma worked together against him.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

To those who knew her, Mothma was kind and caring, yet sometimes forgot herself when dealing in politics, which often seemed to claim importance over everything else in her life. She was a daring woman with charisma and political savvy&mdash;and as such was not devoid of enemies.{{Fact}}

===Clone Wars===
====Political battlefields====
{{Quote|The opposition to this bill must be allowed to speak first!|Mon Mothma, prior to the vote on the bill to increase Republic military spending|<ref name="Pursuit of Peace">{{TCW|Pursuit of Peace}}</ref>}}
[[File:Monmoth.png|thumb|right|215px|Mon Mothma during the Clone Wars]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Republic became embroiled in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] against the union of defecting star systems known as the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> As a senator, Mothma was a proponent of the rights of local systems. She was also friends with fellow Senator Padmé Amidala. Just before the Clone Wars, she became a member of the [[Loyalist Committee/Legends|Loyalist Committee]] along with fellow Senators Bail Organa, Padmé Amidala, [[Fang Zar/Legends|Fang Zar]], and other prominent politicians.{{Fact}} On a night in that year,<ref name="Zillo Beast Date Legends">{{TCWdates|219}}</ref> Mothma was walking with Organa in the corridors of the Senate Building on Coruscant when the gigantic rampaging [[Unidentified Zillo Beast/Legends|Zillo Beast]] [[Zillo Beast incident/Legends|attacked]] it. The [[Zillo Beast/Legends|beast]] was eventually taken down by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic army]].<ref name="Zillo Beast Strikes Back">{{TCW|The Zillo Beast Strikes Back}}</ref>

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="Duchess of Mandalore Date">{{TCWdates|214}}</ref> the neutrality of the planet [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] came into question, with the Senate voting to send an occupying force based on a doctored recording of the deceased [[Deputy Minister/Legends|Deputy Minister]] [[Jerec/Legends|Jerec]]. Mothma attended the session of the Senate when the truthful recording, uncovered by Mandalore's [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]], [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], was broadcast, which resulted in the Senate voting against sending forces to Mandalore.<ref name="Duchess of Mandalore">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref> Later that year,<ref name="Assassin date">{{TCWdates|307}}</ref> Mothma, Organa, and Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] held a [[Alderaan Conference on the Clone War Refugee Crisis|conference]] on Alderaan to discuss the increasing number of refugees from the war. Mothma and Organa greeted Amidala when she arrived and escorted her to her quarters. The conference was later disrupted when the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]], attempted to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] Amidala on behalf of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Ziro Desilijic Tiure]], but her efforts failed due to the intervention of the Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]].<ref name="Assassin">{{TCW|Assassin (episode)}}</ref>

In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Evil Plans Date">{{TCWdates|308}}</ref> Mothma attended a party thrown by Amidala in her [[Naboo Queen (restaurant)|apartment]] in the [[Senate apartment complex/Legends|Senate apartment complex]]. The party was arranged in honor of Senator [[Aang/Legends|Aang]], whom Amidala successfully persuaded to vote in favor of reduced military spending.<ref name="Evil Plans">{{TCW|Evil Plans}}</ref> Later that year,<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides Date">{{TCWdates|310}}</ref> Mothma spoke in a senatorial debate on achieving funding for the production of more [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], arguing against Senator [[Gume Saam/Legends|Gume Saam's]] [[Republic financial reform bill|proposed bill]] to open new lines of credit with the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|Banking Clan]]. She expressed her concern that the bill would result in the deregulation of banks, which was countered by [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] Senator [[Halle Burtoni/Legends|Halle Burtoni]] as a small price to pay for the war effort. The session devolved into loud arguments, leading Amidala to propose [[Confederate–Republic peace initiative/Legends|peace negotiations]] with the Separatists and Organa to table the discussion for later. The Senate's eventual vote on the bill was deliberately sabotaged by a Separatist [[Bombing of Coruscant's central power distribution grid|bombing]] of Courscant's [[Central power distribution grid/Legends|central power distribution grid]], which led to the bill's urgent passage.<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides">{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref>

[[File:Mon Mothma in the Senate.png|thumb|left|300px|Mothma watches Amidala's speech arguing against increased military spending.]]
Debate over increased military funding continued, with Burtoni proposing [[Republic military enhancement bill/Legends|legislation]] to create an additional five million clone troopers. Organa was scheduled to speak in the Senate in opposition to the bill, but was injured by Separatist-hired [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] [[Chata Hyoki/Legends|Chata Hyoki]] and [[Robonino/Legends|Robonino]]. Burtoni and other senators called for the vote to proceed, to which Mothma interjected that the opposition needed its chance to speak first. Mothma watched as Amidala arrived at the Senate in time to deliver her own speech instead, in which she described the harsh circumstances faced by her [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaiden]], [[Teckla Minnau/Legends|Teckla Minnau]], due to the impacts of the war on Republic citizens. Her impassioned speech was met with cheers from the senators,<ref name="Pursuit of Peace" /> although the bill was passed by the Senate.<ref name="Senate Murders">{{TCW|Senate Murders}}</ref>

====Senate Murders====
With Organa, Amidala, and Senator [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]], Mothma championed a [[Reduced military spending bill/Legends|bill]] to reduce military spending and lessen production on clone troopers. Amidala gave a speech in the Senate and afterwards met with Mothma, Organa, Farr, Farr's aide [[Lolo Purs/Legends|Lolo Purs]], and Amidala's [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]. Farr and Mothma both complimented the Naboo senator on her performance over a glass of [[Domaine de la Maison sur le Lac/Legends|Domaine de la Maison sur le Lac]]. Their conversation was interrupted by Burtoni, who accused the senators of being part of a Separatist conspiracy. Amidala and Burtoni briefly debated the merits of diplomacy, prompting Mothma to interject in an effort to calm them down. Farr then escorted Burtoni out of the room, and Mothma redirected the conversation towards praising Amidala's efforts in fighting against increased spending. She praised Farr for his role in leading the efforts, to which the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] stated that he was only trying to do the right thing, expressing regret that he had not done so in earlier years. Mothma assured him that he was doing the right thing presently, after which Organa proposed a toast. After the assembled beings&mdash;aside from Purs&mdash;drank, Farr dropped to the floor, his [[Wine/Legends|wine]] having been [[Rodian-lethal poison|poisoned]] by Purs in retaliation for his reverted attempt to join the Separatists earlier in the war. Purs' guilt in the crime was later revealed and she was arrested.<ref name="Senate Murders" /> 

Mothma had two children, with a [[Jobin's father|male]] partner, she had a son, [[Jobin]].<ref name="Entrenched" /> She also had a daughter, [[Lieda Mothma]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" />

By the end of the Clone Wars, Mothma served as a member of the [[Loyalist Committee/Legends|Loyalist Committee]].<ref name="LoE" /> She later signed the [[Petition of 2000]], along with many other senators, in an effort to request that Chancellor Palpatine reduce his power. The [[Delegation of 2000]] presented the petition to Chancellor Palpatine, but the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] made false promises saying that he would give up his emergency powers and silenced Fang Zar when he tried to speak.<ref name="rots novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>

===Imperial Era===
{{Quote|In fact, when ‘Emperor’ Palpatine decided to arrest me for treason, one of his lapdog Senators informed Bail beforehand. Bail, while pretending to gloat with the swine, sent one of his men to warn me. I got off-planet about two minutes ahead of the ISB agents.|Mon Mothma|<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />}}
[[File:Mon-mothma.jpg|thumb|250px|Mon Mothma was a key member in starting the Rebellion.]]
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Palpatine orchestrated the end of the Clone Wars and [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], with himself as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]].<ref name="rots" /> Shortly afterward, Mothma attended Senator Amidala's [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. She, like the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and Queen [[Apailana/Legends|Apailana]] themselves, did not believe the claim that she had been murdered during the false "[[Showdown on Coruscant|Jedi Rebellion]]."<ref name="TRoDV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

For several months following the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], she urged fellow Organa to publicly speak out against [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine with her. However, she recanted after witnessing the Empire's [[Battle of Kashyyyk (19 BBY)|subjugation]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], fearing that her people might undergo the same oppression. She became aware of the existence of Palpatine's right-hand man, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], whom Organa identified as a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]].<ref name="TRoDV" />

Mothma recognized Palpatine's lust for power and worked strenuously in the Senate to oppose the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] and uphold the principles of the Old Republic within the confines of the legal system. For her efforts, Mothma received the title of [[Senior Senator of the Republic|Senior Senator]], being the last person to do so.<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> She began to broach the subject of a revolution with Organa, who rejected her ideas, momentarily worrying Mothma that her old rival would have her arrested. Organa changed his mind following the [[Ghorman Massacre/Legends|Ghorman Massacre]]<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> in approximately 19 BBY,<ref name="Ghorman Date">{{FactFile|31|TAR 1-4|Grand Moff Tarkin}} states that the [[Ghorman Massacre/Legends|Ghorman Massacre]] took place shortly after [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] [[Declaration of a New Order|declared]] himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> in which hundreds of peaceful protestors were killed by the Empire. Organa maintained the facade of Mothma's rival while secretly transferring weapons, funds, and information to Mothma's burgeoning resistance movement. The two met repeatedly in [[Cantham House/Legends|Cantham House]], Organa's residence on Coruscant, where they discussed the framework of the future [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], Mothma openly defied the Emperor, unlike Bail Organa and other senators who only secretly backed the Rebellion. Her forthright views against the Empire brought her under closer investigation by [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|ISB]], [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR]] and even the Emperor himself, thus preventing her from dabbling in more effective covert efforts to undermine Imperial rule. She continued to use her official channels, senatorial privilege and political contacts to effect change, maintaining the belief that a system of the government, no matter how broken, still has some degree of effectiveness. During these years she frequently met with colleagues on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and other worlds, introduced fruitless measures to grant local systems relief from Imperial policies, and tried to place Senate's oversight on Imperial operations. She also tutored Bail's adopted daughter, Leia Organa, in political and diplomatic affairs, preparing her to succeed her father as Alderaan representative in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] and eventually lead a galaxy-spanning resistance movement.<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

While still serving as a senator, Mothma worked to establish organised resistance cells who were unaware of each other's existence,<ref name="Return of the Jedi novelization">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> including the [[Chandrilan resistance]].<ref name="Rebel Dawn">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> As the Empire began to systematically crush early rebel groups, Mothma and other resistance leaders realised that only a united front would be able to overcome them.<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" />

In approximately [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="Escape Date">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' places Mon Mothma's [[Mon Mothma's escape from Coruscant|escape]] from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] [[Standard month/Legends|months]] before the signing of the [[Corellian Treaty]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].</ref> the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau (ISB)]] eventually discovered Mothma's actions in organizing a rebellion,<ref name="Star Wars Annual 1999">''[[Star Wars Annual 1999]]''</ref> and Palpatine lost patience with the Chandrilan senator,<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /> ordering her arrested for [[Treason/Legends|treason]]. Organa discovered the impending arrest through one of Palpatine's [[Unidentified senator (Bail Organa)|loyal senators]], and pretended to gloat while secretly sending a [[Unidentified male (Bail Organa)|man]] to warn her.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> With the escort of a [[Unidentified bodyguard|bodyguard]],<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /> Mothma [[Mon Mothma's escape from Coruscant|escaped]] Coruscant<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook" /> and pursuing ISB agents by roughly two [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] according to her estimation.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

===Rebellion===
====Early days====
{{Quote|This great struggle is a people's struggle: a struggle between the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor, the cruel and the gentle.|Mon Mothma describing the Rebellion|<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />}}
Shortly after escaping, Mothma met the [[Corellian Resistance/Legends|Corellian Resistance]] operative [[Bria Tharen]]. She shook Tharen's hands and thanked her for her role in persuading Organa to turn away from a pacifistic approach. Tharen considered the moment a high point in her life. On Chandrila, the Emperor's attempt to arrest Mothma was met with protests, resulting in a [[Massacre on Chandrila|massacre]] of the demonstrators.<ref name="Rebel Dawn" /> On the run, Mothma devoted her time to fully building the Alliance using the frameworks she and Organa had discussed. She travelled across [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] to make contact with existing resistance groups establish new ones,<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> and unite rival resistance factions, organizing them into effective and self-sufficient groups.<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> Mothma's fame was both beneficial to her goals but was also a hindrance, as some insurgents did not trust her, fearing that she was an Imperial plant. Mothma faced danger from both rebel groups and Imperial forces.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Organa placed a guard at Mothma's side named [[Malan Tugrina]]. Now a fugitive from Imperial law, she went underground to lead the Rebellion full-time. Chandrila suffered as a result of Mon Mothma’s defiance. The Empire retaliated through numerous punitive measures, including the arrest of Chandrilan politicians and the imposition of heavy tariffs on agrarian exports from the Bormea sector. She became the organization's public face, signing such open proclamations as the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]] and ''[[A Call to Reason]]''.<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /><ref name="Strongholds of Resistance">''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]''</ref>

[[File:Bail_Organa_and_Mon_Mothma.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Mon Mothma and Bail Organa, two of the Alliance's most prominent members]]
Mothma eventually persuaded the three largest groups,<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> her Chandrilan resistance, the Corellian Resistance led by Senator [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], and Organa's [[Alderaanian Resistance]],<ref name="Rebel Dawn" /> to ally with each other in the [[Corellian System Meetings]]. Shortly afterwads,<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> in 2 BBY,<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> the three met on Coruscant for a highly risky meeting in Cantham House, where they agreed to formalize the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

Mothma wrote the [[Corellian Treaty]], in which the three groups pledged to fight the Empire. In its terms, the individual resistance groups would maintain their existing structures and autonomy, while Mothma, with the help of an [[Advisory Council (Alliance)|Advisory Council]], had complete control over supply, recruitment and training, interplanetary communication, intelligence, and space operations. Mothma's decisions were not able to be overruled by other allies. She knew that the upcoming war would demand sacrifices and hard choices, and that she was capable of making them and could not trust others to do so objectively.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Mothma, Organa, and Bel Iblis met to sign the treaty on the planet [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], which was also attended by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], [[Galen Marek]], and his droid [[PROXY]], through whom Leia Organa attended holographically. Marek was the secret [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] of Darth Vader, and had united the rebel leaders in a ploy to eliminate the Emperor's enemies. At the meeting, Organa pledged that the combined individuals would work to fight the Empire with Marek and Kota's help, with Mothma specifically providing soldiers for the upcoming [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The meeting was cut short when an explosion rocked the site of the signing and the emergence of Imperial [[Cold weather assault trooper|Snowtroopers]]. Vader entered, having betrayed Marek. Mothma and the other senators were captured and taken to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]].<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

Marek, however, had escaped, and with the help of his [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], he [[Battle on Death Star I|traveled]] to the Death Star construction site to rescue his allies. Mothma, Bel Iblis, Organa, and Kota were brought before the Emperor, where Palaptine demanded that they share the names of their other allies and promised to have them all publicly executed. His threats were interrupted by the arrival of Marek, whom Vader [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|dueled]]. Marek defeated his former master and entered the chamber where the senators were imprisoned. Palpatine attempted to seduce Marek to take Vader's place as his apprentice, but Marek chose to fight the Emperor instead. He was able to subdue the Emperor initially, which allowed Eclipse, piloting the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', to land inside the chamber. Marek was forced to hold off the Emperor's [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] to allow the Rebels to escape, sacrificing his life in the process. As Vader and Palpatine looked upon Marek's corpse, Vader swore to continue hunting down the escapees, with Palpatine worried that they would prove to be their undoing.<ref name="TFU" />

====Alliance Head of State====
The Rebel leaders met on the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], Marek's homeworld, where Leia chose the [[House of Marek|Marek family]] crest as the [[Alliance Starbird|symbol]] of the official Rebel Alliance.<ref name="TFU" /> Due to her reputation for honesty, Mothma was unanimously elected [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|Chief of State]] of the Alliance.<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> Although the position essentially functioned as that of an elected dictator, she had included a clause in the Corellian Treaty in which Alliance leaders would have a majority vote every two years for their leadership, although no other candidates ever stood for election against her. Mothma had an active role in [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]], actively directing the war effort.Mothma's days were mostly spent in conferences, with daily meetings with the [[Supreme Allied Commanders]], along with informal meetings with other stakeholders such as commanders, subcommittees, and tasks forces.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

During the early days of the Rebellion, Mothma worked to organize the Rebellion into a viable [[Alliance Military/Legends|military force]].<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> The Alliance rapidly expanded after the signing of the treaty, recruiting further groups to the cause after careful vetting, receiving anonymous donations from sympathetic wealthy families and corporations.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> She also took a leadership role in many important missions. These included gaining the [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]] for the Alliance and [[Operation Skyhook|finding the plans]] for the Death Star. Captain [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]] acted as her right hand man until his death.{{Fact}} 

At one point, Mothma negotiated with the inhabitants of the planet [[Sanctuary/Legends|Sanctuary]], and agreed to their terms in which they would join the Alliance but be permitted not to take up arms.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Shortly after the signing of the Corellian Treaty, Mothma saw the need to clarify the Rebellion's objectives to the galaxy and reframe their narrative, as they were perceived as [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], criminals, and anarchists. She wrote the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]], which was directly addressed to the Emperor and listed the broad crimes of the Empire along with the goals of the Alliance. Millions of holo-copies were made and distributed by [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]], and within days of its publication, copies could be found on every planet in the Empire. In response, several systems openly declared their allegiance to the Rebellion. Mothma attempted to stop these so-called [[Secession Worlds]] from doing so, but was too late to save them from Imperial retaliation. However, they did manage to transfer their resources, military power, and weaponry to the Alliance beforehand. The overall impact of the Declaration was better than Mothma could have hoped for, as it alerted many in the galaxy to the existence of the Rebellion. while also developing their sympathy.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

At one point, Mothma visited the [[Atrivis sector/Legends|Atrivis sector]] to link the [[Atrivis Resistance Group/Legends|Atrivis Resistance Group (ARG)]], who were unaware of the wider rebellion outside of their sector, to the Alliance. The group's leaders were hesitant, but Mothma was suitably persuasive, highlighting the benefits of a potential galaxy-wide communications network and the effectiveness of centralized leadership for the Rebellion. She acknowledged that this meant some loss of control for the group in their own decision making, but argued that it was essential to combat the strength of the Empire. Mothma also proposed to make their base on the planet [[Generis/Legends|Generis]] into a key communications station to link Outer Rim resistance groups together, and to establish a starfighter base there, which appealed to the ARG, as they had no fighters of their own. There was some argument amongst the leaders, but they ultimately signed the [[Treaty of Generis]] and joined the Alliance.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Mothma was not immune to the watchful eyes of Rebel [[Counter-Intelligence]] [[Security]], who had installed two of their agents as Mothma's aides. The Chief of State incorrectly suspected that only [[Unidentified aide|one of her aides]] was an agent, but the individual in question was not.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Mothma gave command of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] to the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]], sending him directly to the [[Telaris system/Legends|Telaris system]] to enhance and prepare the fleet.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

During that time, she worked with a Bothan to insert her nephew, [[Kell Bircher]], into the Empire as a spy. In the chaos after the Battle of Yavin, he was able to gain the rank of elite pilot, although he later crashed his ship aboard ''[[Home One]]'' and revealed the plot to [[Stealth Squadron|Gray Flight]].<ref name="SW 12 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 12|''Star Wars'' (2013) 12]]</ref>

====Early victories====
The Alliance's early victories were found in hit-and-run guerilla strikes against the Empire. Mothma advised caution against larger strikes, knowing that the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] could not match the might of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. The Alliance was forced into battle before they were ready due to the revelation of the Death Star, which was capable of destroying entire planets.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> In their first [[Battle of Toprawa|victory]], Rebel spies were able to steal the [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] for the Death Star, hoping to exploit a potential weakness. Before the plans could be safely taken to the [[Great Temple/Legends|Rebel Base]] on the moon [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], the Death Star was used to [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destroy]] Alderaan,<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Bail Organa was among the casualties, which led to an imbalance in the Alliance's leadership. Without Organa to counter her, Garm Bel Iblis thought that Mothma was assuming dictatorial powers over the Alliance and intended to set herself up in Palpatine's place. He left the Rebellion in protest, forming a long-lasting rift.<ref name="Heir to the Empire Sourcebook" />

In the immediate aftermath of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], in which the newly recruited Rebel [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] destroyed the Death Star,<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV" /> Mothma oversaw the award ceremony for the starfighter pilot [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]], where she presented the [[Star of Alderaan/Legends|Star of Alderaan]] citation in recognition for his actions during the battle.<ref name="X-wing">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref>

====Post-Yavin====
Two months after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Mothma reflected on the fledgling rebellion with Leia Organa. Mothma assigned the former senator to a secret mission, telling her to form a team with only two objectives, find a double-agent or a new home for the Alliance leadership. She handed Organa the only copy of a protocol that she had prepared herself.<ref name="SW 1 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 1|''Star Wars'' (2013) 1]]</ref> Shortly afterward, Han Solo was assigned to meet one of Mothma's contacts on Imperial Center.<ref name="SW 2 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 2|''Star Wars'' (2013) 2]]</ref> Her contact, though, betrayed Solo to Imperial Security and was killed by Solo in turn. Mothma later met with Organa to hear her report on the secret operation. Organa requested Mothma's clearance codes so she could start leaking information. Organa also reported an issue with [[Prithi]], one of the pilots of [[Stealth Squadron]]. Mothma responded by asking whose problem it was: for fellow pilot [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], or for Organa herself.<ref name="SW 3 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 3|''Star Wars'' (2013) 3]]</ref> Soon after, Mothma was present on the bridge of the [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']] when Gray Flight launched. She prevented a Mon Calamari commander from firing on the unauthorized departure. When the commander asked whether or not the order was in service to the Rebellion, Mothma replied that every breath she took was in rebellion to the Empire.<ref name="SW 4 (DH)">[[Star Wars (2013) 4|''Star Wars'' (2013) 4]]</ref>

When Admiral [[Harkov]], a high-ranking officer in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], contacted the Rebel Alliance to talk about his defection, Mon Mothma personally traveled to a secret meeting with him to negotiate the price of his services.

At some point between [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]] submitted a report on [[Operation Cobolt]] directly to Mothma. In it, Madine requested Mothma's permission to recommend the fallen Colonels [[Toombs]] and [[Anna Seertay]] for posthumous promotion and commendation.<ref name="Operation Cobolt">{{WEGCite|story=General Madine's Report on Operation Cobolt|book=The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook}}</ref>

Post-Yavin, [[Executive Secretary]] and [[Master Historian]] [[Arhul Hextrophon/Legends|Arhul Hextrophon]] was commissioned by Mothma to compile a detailed report about the Alliance, including its history, structure, members, and equipment. Hextrophon submitted a condensed version to Mothma, hoping that it would be satisfactory given the limited time he had to prepare it. Mothma wrote a response in which she praised the report, particularly as a legacy of the Alliance's actions to pass on to the next generation. She expressed her paranoia about the Emperor and his power and feared that the Rebellion would struggle to succeed in overthrowing him. Additionally, she described her dreams in which she saw a lone boy fighting against Vader and the Emperor. She believed that all of the Alliance's efforts depended on him.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

In 3 ABY,<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> the Alliance suffered a significant defeat to the Empire at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. Mothma's son, [[Corporal/Legends|Coroporal]] Jobin, recorded a message for his mother shortly before the battle. He was killed by Vader in the fray, but was able to pass his message on to a comrade.<ref name="Entrenched" />

[[File:Mothmaleadingbriefing.png|thumb|right|275px|Mon Mothma led the Rebel Briefing shortly before defeating the Empire in the Battle of Endor.]]
In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Bothan spies discovered the near-completion of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] and learned that the Emperor himself would be onboard.<ref name="rotj" /> Mothma prepared herself to deliver the briefing on the mission. Shortly beforehand, aboard [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']], she received Jobin's recorded message and played it, wondering why it had taken so long to reach her. After viewing it, General Madine confirmed to Mothma that her son had been killed at Hoth.<ref name="Entrenched" /> In the briefing, Mothma outlined the Bothans' intelligence, including that they had located the Death Star II in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], the superweapon was not yet operational, the station was relatively unprotected due to how spread thin the Imperial fleet was. She emphasised that Palpatine would personally be aboard the Death Star and that many Bothans had been killed in uncovering the intelligence. Mothma watched as Ackbar and Madine then gave their own briefings regarding the logistics of the upcoming [[Battle of Endor/Legends|battle]], and as the [[Endor strike team/Legends|Endor strike team]] was finalized, led by Solo.<ref name="rotj" />

Mothma was also uncomfortable with elements of the plan itself, feeling that the Alliance would be damaged by resorting to assassination. Her demeanor remained steady, however, and the Rebel forces were inspired by her resolve.{{Fact}} Unbeknownst to Mothma, Palpatine had allowed the intelligence to leak to the Rebellion in a plot to lure them into their final destruction.<ref name="rotj" /> Mothma's dream about a lone figure facing Vader and the Emperor<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> came true during the Battle of Endor, where Luke Skywalker faced them and turned his father back to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]], resulting in the death of the Emperor. Lando Calrissian also destroyed the Death Star II, securing the Alliance's victory.<ref name="rotj" />

After the battle, she turned the Rebel Alliance into a transitional government&mdash;the [[Alliance of Free Planets]]. During this period, she built diplomatic and military coalitions to fight the remnants of the Empire, as well as such threats as the [[Ssi-ruu]]k during the [[Bakura Incident|Bakura crisis]], the [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]], and the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]].{{Fact}}

===Chief of State of the New Republic===
{{Quote|That is our goal: To become the New Republic in fact as well as name.|Mon Mothma|<ref name="htte">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>}}
[[File:MonMothma-NEGTC.png|thumb|left|200px|Mon Mothma as Chief of State.]]
As the Alliance transitioned into the New Republic, Mothma became its Chief of State. For eleven years she led the fledgling democratic republic, holding together the many factions that flocked to its membership. As the New Republic weathered one major military threat after another, Mothma's charisma and leadership proved essential.

During Mothma's time as [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]], the Republic reclaimed Coruscant from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Mothma then had to deal with the artificial [[Krytos virus]], a biological weapon left behind by Imperial Intelligence that affected only nonhumans and was only curable by massive amounts of [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]]. The fallout from the Krytos Virus seriously tested the new government.<ref name="X-Wing: The Krytos Trap" /> During the hunt for warlord Zsinj an aide named Tolokai, another bodyguard, had undergone brainwashing. He attacked Malan first, driving a knife into his chest, then her. As Mon Mothma fled down the stairs she fell and was wounded badly. Before Tolokai could raise a knife, Malan surprised him and they tumbled down the stairs. His death saddened her deeply.<ref name="SC">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref>

Mothma always put the Republic before her personal life, even going so far as to advocate for Leia Organa to accept [[Hapan]] Prince [[Isolder]]'s offer of marriage to strengthen the Republic. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], she presided over the wedding of Leia to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].<ref name="PL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref> Shortly after, a painting containing a [[Shadowcast]] key for the Rebellion's spy network that had been thought destroyed with Alderaan resurfaced on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. She sent newly married Leia Organa and Han Solo along with [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] to recover the painting.<ref name="TG">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref>

[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] engaged in a campaign that nearly toppled the Republic. At about the same time as Thrawn was engaging in his campaign, she faced trouble within her own government&mdash;a group of Bothans nearly forced her from office, before the lead [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]], [[Borsk Fey'lya]] was found out. After Thrawn's death, the revived Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], in a new clone body attacked the Republic, driving it from Coruscant to [[Da Soocha V]]<ref name="RS">{{JournalCite|7|Retreat from Coruscant}}</ref><ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref> and later to [[Nespis VIII]].<ref name="DEII">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]''</ref> Palpatine was defeated, but the cost in terms of loss of life and other damage was huge.

Mothma supported Luke Skywalker in his efforts to reestablish the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi Order]] to protect and guide the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. She gave her official sanction to Skywalker's efforts to find and recruit potential Jedi. Mothma also arranged for Skywalker to be given the former Rebel base on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4's]] moon as a home for the new Jedi school.<ref name="JS">''[[Jedi Search]]''</ref>

In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] Mon Mothma contacted [[Kyle Katarn]] and [[Jan Ors]] to investigate an Imperial Remnant base on [[Kejim]]. After they returned with an [[Artusian crystal]] in her [[Chief of State's office|office]], she [[Battle of Artus Prime|sent]] them to [[Artus Prime]] to investigate further.<ref name="JK:JO">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>

Unlike her years in the Alliance, Mothma did not stay hidden in safety. During a diplomatic visit to Coruscant, Ambassador [[Furgan]], an ambassador from [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], threw what appeared to be a drink on Mothma's face as an insulting send-off gesture. This "drink" turned out to be nanomachines that slowly affected Mothma. Mothma decided to resign her post as Chief of State as her condition worsened, and guided the council to appoint Leia Organa Solo to succeed her in office.

===Retirement===
[[File:Maramon.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mon Mothma worked late into her life with New Republic Intelligence.]]
The condition nearly killed her, but at the last minute Mothma was saved by the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Cilghal]] who used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to cleanse her body. Without the nanomachines in her body, Mothma's condition improved. Within a few weeks she was standing again, something that Leia never thought she'd see Mothma accomplish after her ailment. Leia tried to convince Mothma to become Chief of State again, but Mothma refused&mdash;feeling that the time had come for her to step aside.

Despite her improvement, Mothma never completely recovered. For the most part, she retired from public life. However, in [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], during the [[Almanian Uprising]], she became acting Chief of State while Leia Organa Solo, the current Chief of State, led [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] and a fleet to [[Almania]] to find her brother, and rescue him from the megalomaniac [[Kueller]]. She later resigned when Leia returned.<ref name="TNR">''[[The New Rebellion]]''</ref>

In [[18 ABY/Legends|18 ABY]], during the [[Corellian Crisis|First Corellian Uprising]], Mon Mothma asked Luke Skywalker to help Lando Calrissian find a wife. Later, she suggested that Luke and Lando travel to Bakura to find [[Gaeriel Captison]].

In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], she was present at the signing of the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|Bastion Accords]],<ref name="EC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> and was a guest of honor at [[Wedding of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade|the wedding]] of Luke Skywalker and [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]], where she arrived with [[Talon Karrde]], Borsk Fey'lya and [[Elegos A'Kla]]. Jedi [[Kam Solusar]] showed Mothma her seats and left her as some Imperials attacked.<ref name="U">''[[Star Wars: Union]]''</ref>

===Death===
Her condition continued to worsen, albeit slowly, and shortly before the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] she died quietly in her sleep. In honor of her courage and bravery throughout the years, a New Republic [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] was given the name [[Mon Mothma (Imperial-class)|''Mon Mothma'']].<ref name="SbS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Settling scores is no way to govern a galaxy.|Mon Mothma, to Ackbar and Borsk Fey'lya|<ref name="atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>}}
Although Mothma was elected senator during the decline of the Republic, she served vigorously and with integrity<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> and passion.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> She was wary of the increasing amount of power that Supreme Chancellor Palpatine was gathering, and along with 1,999 other Senators, signed a petition calling for him to relinquish his emergency powers as the Clone Wars neared their end.<ref name="rotsnovel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Mothma correctly foresaw the fall of the Old Republic and was outspoken in sharing her views prior to its Imperial transformation.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

Realizing that the Senate was quickly losing its last vestiges of political influence,<ref name="db">{{DB|character|monmothma|Mothma, Mon}}</ref> she met with other Senators to discuss what options were available to them if they were to oppose the Supreme Chancellor.<ref name="rotsnovel" /> After Palpatine reformed the Republic into a Galactic Empire Mothma continued to oppose his policies,<ref name="db" /> and did not hide her anger or dismay from him.<ref name="Dark Lord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> She went underground and began openly resisting the Empire when its outrages became too difficult to ignore.<ref name="db" /> Mothma considered every breath she took to be in rebellion to the Empire.<ref name="SW 4 (DH)" />

She was not comfortable with the idea of a "secret council" as it "reeked of the Empire", in her words, but with the Alliance on its last legs soon after the Battle of Yavin, Mothma formed one with Organa and tasked her with a new protocol.<ref name="SW 1 (DH)" /> Mothma believed that she was the only one capable of making the hard choices required of the leader of a galaxy-wide rebellion, though she detested the concept of absolute power, which meant that she included the clause in the Corellian Treaty for the election of an Alliance leader every two years.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> 

As a strategist, Mothma supported a "stateless" strategy; while many military minds of the Alliance proposed to gradually conquer the galaxy (starting from Mon Calamari) Mothma repeatedly disagreed, preferring the Alliance as an entity without a definite homeworld to become a target.<ref name="atlas" /> She also delegated highly skilled and qualified people into key roles, which had the flow-on effect of encouraging all Rebel military personnel to follow orders while still thinking independently. Additionally, Mothma requested and heeded the advice of those around her, inspired by her values of respect and loyalty.<ref name="The Star Wars Sourcebook" /> Mothma often said little during her daily meetings with Alliance members, but was able to keep them more focused and productive than others thought possible.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

When Bria Tharen met Mothma, she was impressed by the senator's quiet dignity, unswerving resolution and formidable intelligence. The operative considered their meeting a high point in her life.<ref name="Rebel Dawn" />

As Chief of State of the Alliance, Mothma viewed her duty as being to mobilize the energies and resources of the Alliance into supporting, maintaining, and expanding the war effort.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> Although she opposed assassinations as a tool of the state, she was willing to agree to them in special circumstances. While nowhere near as ruthless as Palpatine, Mon Mothma was pragmatic enough not to shy away from using tactics that were not always entirely moral or above-board to ensure the Rebel Alliance's survival.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /><ref name="Edge">[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

[[File:Manybothansdied.png|thumb|left|200px|Mothma felt heavy responsibility for the deaths of Alliance agents.]]
Mothma was a stern and stately woman,<ref name="db" /> and as the Chief of State of the Rebel Alliance,<ref name="Allegiance">[[Allegiance (novel)|''Allegiance'']]</ref> she felt responsible for the many deaths that were met by Alliance forces. When lives were at stake, she was unwilling to hand over responsibility for them, and consequently held onto power in order to ensure that the heavy responsibility was hers alone.<ref name="tlc">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> When a [[Blue Squadron (Bothan)|number]] of Bothan Alliance [[Agent/Legends|agents]] died [[Raid on the Suprosa|securing]] the [[Death Star II plans|technical readouts]] of the Empire's second Death Star, Mothma felt their losses heavily, nearly losing face while addressing the Alliance prior to an attack on the battle station.<ref name="rotj" /> Firm in her convictions, however, she led the briefing despite having learned a moment earlier of the [[Death/Legends|death]] of her son, Jobin.<ref name="Entrenched" />

Mothma's siphoning of power was misinterpreted by her peer, Garm Bel Iblis, as a desire to rule the galaxy.<ref name="dfr">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref> When Mothma earlier led the Chandrilan Resistance against the Empire, her pacifist methods were less direct than Bel Iblis's confrontational modus operandi.<ref name="garmdb">{{DB|character|garmbeliblis|Bel Iblis, Garm}}</ref> Nine years after a falling-out with Bel Iblis, she welcomed him into the New Republic, but was too proud to address the issue of their previous hostility or to admit any past failings. She overcame this pride, however, when the Empire was [[Siege of Coruscant|laying siege]] to the New Republic's home base of Coruscant and she asked Bel Iblis to lead its defense.<ref name="tlc" />

Towards the end of her life, Mothma continued to support her friends in the New Republic despite her retirement and failing health. She stepped in as acting Chief of State of the government to aid an overwhelmed Leia Organa Solo during the Almanian Uprising,<ref name="TNR" /> and [[18 ABY/Legends|one year later]], offered political advice to Luke Skywalker regarding his [[New Jedi Order]].<ref name="ambush">''[[Ambush at Corellia]]''</ref>

==Skills and abilities==
Mothma's skill as a politician and mediator was considered more beneficial to the Alliance High Command than her not-inconsiderable military understanding.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

==Equipment==
When travelling through potentially hostile environments, Mothma used a modified [[Freerunner/Legends|freerunner]], fitted with heavy armor plating and [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], as a [[Transport/Legends|transport]].<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Certainly people are always very envious of me. When I join a new theater company, the other actors look down the program, see my ''Return of the Jedi'' credit and say, 'Oh, you were part of ''Star Wars''.' I smile and say, 'Yes, but only for twenty-six and a half seconds.'|Caroline Blakiston|<ref name="galaxy12">[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 12|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 12]]</ref>}}
Mon Mothma was created for [[Richard Marquand]]'s [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]<ref name="rotj" /> and made her first appearance in the film's [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]], written by [[James Kahn]] and published earlier in the same year.<ref name="rotj novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]</ref> In the film, she was portrayed by [[Caroline Blakiston]], who was cast while working on a television series in [[Wikipedia:Manchester|Manchester]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]]. Costume designers from the film visited Blakiston in her Manchester hotel to fit her and discuss her character's hairstyle, but ultimately decided to use her own short red hair. Blakiston was given Mothma's lines for the character's brief appearance in the film, but upon arriving on the set to film her scene, was informed that Mothma's lines had been completely changed. She had to quickly learn a new monologue, which she found stressful, particularly due to the unique ''[[Star Wars]]'' language it contained, such as "Bothan".<ref name="Blakiston interview">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/05/caroline-blakiston-interview-mon-mothma.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Caroline Blakiston interview &#124; Mon Mothma &#124; Star Wars}}</ref> While performing the role, Blakiston attempted to create a sense of background for the character, seeking inspiration in the classical underpinnings of the ''Star Wars'' saga. She interpreted "Mon Mothma" to mean "Moon Mother", and thus saw her character as cool and calm.<ref name="Knightley">{{InsiderCite|75|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of Star Wars)|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of ''Star Wars'')}}</ref> After filming her single scene in the movie, Blakiston returned to re-record her dialogue when it was discovered that pigeons roosting in the set were audible in the initial recording.<ref name="db" />

Despite appearing in the film for less than thirty seconds,<ref name="rotj" /><ref name="galaxy12" /> Mothma's character and role in the Rebellion were later fleshed out in various [[Star Wars comic books|comic books]], novels and reference books.<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="marvel88">[[Star Wars (1977) 88|''Star Wars'' (1977) 88]]</ref><ref name="marvel90">[[Star Wars (1977) 90|''Star Wars'' (1977) 90]]</ref> [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[1991]]'s novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' introduced her as the Chief of State of the Rebel Alliance's successor government, the New Republic,<ref name="htte" /> a position that Leia Organa Solo succeeded her in in [[Kevin J. Anderson]]'s [[1994]] novel ''[[Champions of the Force]]''.<ref name="cotf">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref> ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', published in [[2005]], established that Mothma passed away in her sleep in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Blakiston is aware of and intrigued by the fact that the character she portrayed became a major character in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]],<ref name="Blakiston interview" /> the intrigue stemming from the strong personality she believed Mothma to possess. She sees Mothma as an archetypal figure similar to Darth Vader and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].<ref name="Knightley" />

2005 also saw Mothma appear in [[George Lucas]]'s film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]<ref name="rots" /> where she was played by [[Genevieve O'Reilly]], who was cast due to her resemblance to Blakiston. O'Reilly carefully studied Blakiston's performance in order to capture the character's voice and mannerisms.<ref name="db" /> O'Reilly's speaking scenes were ultimately [[Content cut from Star Wars|cut]] from the film, but were included in its [[Star Wars home video releases#Star_Wars_Episode_III:_Revenge_of_the_Sith|DVD release]]<ref name="dvd">{{Film|III}} [[Star Wars home video releases#Star_Wars_Episode_III:_Revenge_of_the_Sith|DVD]]</ref> and appear in the film's [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]].<ref name="rotsnovel" /> She appears as Mothma in a non-speaking role in the final version of the film.<ref name="rots" /> Blakiston herself wrote to Lucas to ask if she could appear in the film as Mon Mothma's grandmother, but did not receive a response.<ref name="Blakiston interview" />

[[2010|Five years after]] the release of Episode III, Mothma began appearing in the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', where she was voiced by [[Kath Soucie]].<ref name="Senate Murders" /> Several actors have voiced the character in other Expanded Universe works: [[Natalia Nogulich]] in the [[Return of the Jedi (radio)|''Return of the Jedi'' radio drama]],<ref name="rotjradio">{{RJRadio|Pattern and Web}}</ref> [[Peggy Roberts-Hope]] in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s ''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''<ref name="DF">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref> and ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]'',<ref name="JK:MotS">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]''</ref> [[Carolyn Seymour]] in the video games ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''<ref name="JK:JO" /> and ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'',<ref name="EaW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref> [[Ann Patricio]] in the [[Dark Empire: The Collector's Edition|''Dark Empire'' audio adaptations]],<ref name="deaudio">''[[Dark Empire: The Collector's Edition]]''</ref> and [[Chris Forth]] in the [[Dark Forces: The Collector's Trilogy|''Dark Forces'' audio adaptations]].<ref name="darkforcesaudio">''[[Dark Forces: The Collector's Trilogy]]''</ref>

Although some Expanded Universe works claim that Mothma represented the entire Bormea sector in the Imperial Senate,<ref name="adventure">{{JournalCite|3|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> others assert that [[Zafiel Snopps]] was concurrently the Imperial Senator from [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]].<ref name="Snopps">{{WEGCite|story=An Old Flame in Need...|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref> Corulag is in the Bormea sector.<ref name="corulag">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> The ''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]'' erroneously states that Mothma was at one time possessed by the spirit of [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]].<ref name="jatm">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

Originally, Mon Mothma was intended to die in ''Champions of the Force'' from Furgan's nano-destroyers, but this was rejected by Lucasfilm.<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref>

While sources like the defunct official [[Databank (original)|Databank]] of [[StarWars.com]] and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' gave Mon Mothma's height as 1.5 meters,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="db" /> both actresses who portrayed her were actually taller. In ''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'', Mothma was seen standing next to Crix Madine, who was confirmed to measure 1.7 meters tall, and looked just as tall as him. Mothma's [[Clone Cards|Clone Card]] on StarWars.com, however, listed her height as a more realistic 1.7 meters, despite the official [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|encyclopedia]]&mdash;hosted on the same website&mdash;still gave her height as 1.5 meters.<ref name="SWE">{{SWE|characters|mon-mothma|Mon Mothma}}</ref>

===Non-canon content===
Sometime after Mothma was put on the top of the most wanted list by Palpatine, she was located by agents of the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]]. Although they managed to capture Mothma's entourage, Mothma herself was able to escape. Mothma soon tried to escape to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] on the [[Blackjack (YT-1300 light freighter)|''Blackjack'']], but was unable to make it onboard as she was captured by fellow [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Pel Talon]]. Talon locked her up in the archaic dungeon of his own personal castle, hoping to exploit her capture at a later time. He was unable to do so, however, as Mothma was rescued by a group of Rebels including [[Jax Keyn]], [[Trillia (pilot)|Trillia]], and [["Mouse" Temple]].
